title: Improving pyelonephritis on ceftriaxone; only oral beta-lactam options remain

clinical_review.notes: Owner clinical review: cases look good.

story: A 52-year-old woman with acute pyelonephritis is on IV ceftriaxone, hospital day 3. She has been afebrile for 36 hours, is eating and drinking, and her vital signs are normal. The urine E. coli is susceptible to ceftriaxone and to cefazolin at the urinary surrogate breakpoint, but resistant to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and ciprofloxacin.

expected_findings.summary: Clinical criteria for an oral switch are met, but the only susceptible oral options for pyelonephritis are beta-lactams.

acceptable_answers: Switch to an oral cephalosporin the cefazolin surrogate supports (for example cefpodoxime), completing a longer total course than with a fluoroquinolone, and document the reasoning.
Continue IV ceftriaxone to complete the course, given that oral beta-lactams are considered less effective for pyelonephritis than fluoroquinolones or TMP-SMX.
Discuss with the team or infectious diseases before choosing between the two.
reference_answer: Flag the patient as meeting clinical IV to PO criteria and present both options: an oral cephalosporin with a longer total duration, or completing IV therapy. Either is defensible; the finding should not claim a single correct choice.
rationale: An ambiguous case: reasonable pharmacists differ. She meets clinical switch criteria, but the susceptible oral agents are beta-lactams, which the 2011 IDSA guideline considers less effective for pyelonephritis, recommending a longer course if used. Nitrofurantoin does not reach renal tissue. The newer IDSA complicated UTI guideline may change this balance; the owner reviews it before this case is approved.

citations.supports: Oral beta-lactams for pyelonephritis: less effective than other agents, longer duration when used.
Current guidance on oral step-down for complicated UTI and pyelonephritis; owner to confirm.
Cefazolin as a surrogate for oral cephalosporins in urinary isolates.
Stewardship programs promoting timely IV to oral transition once criteria are met.
